notes: Hook checked: a 0.02 ohm rise against the wobble of repeat readings is a fair question, matches lesson i1 (which asks for the standard deviation of repeat readings to judge it) and research note R3; no change.

oneBreath failed on overclaims and was corrected in topic.json: "Every reading you take is a little different from the last" is not true (repeat readings on a 0.01 ohm step often repeat, as lesson i1 piles show); now "Repeat readings of the same thing rarely all agree", in line with R3 (repeating gives a randomly different result).
oneBreath: "Readings in the order taken show whether a change is wear or just noise" overclaimed (noise alone still makes a fitted line lean, R13 and idea i4); now "help show".

oneBreath: "a failure rate tells you what share ... should still be working" holds only for a constant failure rate and as a statistical expectation (R14, R15, R17); now "a steady failure rate tells you roughly what share".

Was: Every reading you take is a little different from the last, and statistics is how you work with that wobble. The middle and the spread of repeat readings tell you what a reading really is, how far to trust it and when one is unusual. Readings in the order taken show whether a change is wear or just noise, and a failure rate tells you what share of equipment should still be working after a given time.
